findings.title: Decoder assumes exactly two-character grant shortcuts
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires encodedContext.length() == 6 and then splits the prefix as 2 chars for session type, 2 for token type, and 2 for grant type. However OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is documented as usually a 3-letter shortcut and does not enforce a 2-character length. A custom grant factory returning a valid 3-character shortcut (for example "abc") will generate an ID such as "onrtabc:<uuid>", which this decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException. Any endpoint that later parses token context from such an access token will fail. Either enforce exactly two characters when collecting shortcuts in the factory or make the encoding/decoding format length-independent.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId checks the wrong substring and has an inverted comparison
findings.body: The matcher reads items[0].substring(3, 5) for the grant-type shortcut, but the grant shortcut occupies characters 4-5 (0-based indexes 4 and 5) in the 6-character prefix. It also returns false when the substring equals the expected shortcut, which is the inverse of the intended assertion. As a result, the matcher accepts token IDs whose grant shortcut is not the expected one and the updated expectCodeToToken()/expectRefresh()/device/CIBA assertions do not actually validate the encoded grant type. It can also throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException if the prefix is shorter than 5 characters.

findings.title: Constructor checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") a second time instead of validating rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, and encodeTokenId() would concatenate it as the literal text "null" into the token ID. The error message for the repeated grantType check is also misleading. This should use rawTokenId in the second requireNonNull call.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: Adding a non-default abstract getShortcut() method to the public OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface is a source and binary compatibility break. Existing custom grant-type factories compiled against the previous interface will not implement this method and can fail at startup with AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() calls gtf.getShortcut() for every registered grant factory. Provide a default implementation or otherwise handle legacy factories without breaking startup.

findings.title: Removal of public Context copy constructor breaks extension callers
findings.body: The public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context) copy constructor was removed from the Context class. This is a source and binary compatibility break for any custom grant implementation that used it to clone/modify a context. The new grantType field could simply be copied in that constructor, so removing the constructor is unnecessary for the feature.
